turns.question: Why did I miss this shot?
turns.player_text:
It looks like the ball came down short of the basket. The view doesn’t confirm whether it touched the rim, though.

You did get a good bend and rise through your legs, so I wouldn’t change your knee bend based on this shot. The clip doesn’t tell us what caused the short arrival. Did it feel short as it left your hand?

turns.question: Can you visually show me what I should improve?
turns.player_text:
Look at your shooting arm in these frames. Near release, your elbow is still bent; in the early follow-through, your arm has straightened toward the basket. That extension is worth keeping.

For now, use that finish as a checkpoint: let your arm extend comfortably toward the hoop rather than forcing more knee bend. I can’t point to a specific change that would have fixed this miss from these frames alone.

turns.question: What should I practice, and can you recommend an instructional video?
turns.player_text:
Practice a comfortable free-throw routine rather than changing your mechanics: use your usual setup, pick a spot on the rim, and shoot with a comfortable rhythm. Keep the relaxed arm extension we saw.

Try one set of five free throws. Notice where each ball lands and whether the routine felt comfortable; use that as a baseline, not a test you have to pass.

Fundamentals of the Free Throw · Jr. NBA
https://jr.nba.com/video/fundamentals-of-the-free-throw/

Shoot free throws using your usual comfortable setup, a chosen spot on the rim, and the same relaxed rhythm each time.

Notice where each ball lands and whether your routine feels comfortable; use the set as a baseline.

turns.question: What should I keep about my current technique?
turns.player_text:
Keep the bend and rise you had through your legs, and the way your shooting arm extended toward the basket in your follow-through. Both are worth preserving rather than forcing a new motion.

This shot doesn’t give me a reason to rebuild your technique. Keep your usual setup too, if it feels comfortable, and let the finish happen naturally.
